sentences.en: And his friend, Kenneth Colby, became one of his first targets.

sentences.zh: 他开始在公共场合和专业会议上抨击科尔比博士。

sentences.en: And he would say, this is a wicked thing to do.

sentences.en: These programs could take a long time to figure things out.
sentences.zh: 这些程序可能需要很长时间才能弄清楚事情。

sentences.en: It has been a tedious three-year project.
sentences.zh: 这是一个枯燥的三年项目。

sentences.en: The computer now knows about 300 words.
sentences.zh: 计算机现在认识大约300个单词。

sentences.en: Still, Paul Martin is convinced computers can learn.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，保罗·马丁仍然坚信计算机可以学习。

sentences.en: But starting in the 1980s and 90s, there were new breakthroughs in natural language processing.
sentences.zh: 但从20世纪80年代和90年代开始，自然语言处理领域出现了新的突破。

sentences.en: Scientists began relying on statistical methods.
sentences.zh: 科学家们开始依赖统计方法。

sentences.en: Taking documents or recordings of language and performing statistics on things like, how often does one word come after another?
sentences.zh: 获取文档或语言录音，并对诸如“一个词出现在另一个词之后的频率”之类的事情进行统计。

sentences.en: Or how often does this sort of triplet of words occur?
sentences.zh: 或者这种三词组合出现的频率是多少？

sentences.en: And then in the 2000s and 2010s, researchers began using what are called deep neural networks.
sentences.zh: 然后在21世纪的头两个十年，研究人员开始使用所谓的深度神经网络。

sentences.en: They're trained using the huge amounts of data that only became possible with the rise of the Internet.
sentences.zh: 它们使用只有随着互联网兴起才可能获得的海量数据进行训练。

sentences.en: So now we can, like, take every single web page online and process the language in it and have the neural network analyze the language.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们可以获取网上的每一个网页，处理其中的语言，并让神经网络分析这些语言。

sentences.en: And they work so much better than anything that came before.
sentences.zh: 它们的效果比以往任何技术都要好得多。

sentences.en: And these techniques Mitchell is describing, they've been applied to chatbots specifically.
sentences.zh: 而米切尔所描述的这些技术，已经被专门应用于聊天机器人。

sentences.en: They might be trained on actual conversations, recorded conversations.
sentences.zh: 它们可能是通过真实的对话，即录制的对话进行训练的。

sentences.en: Sometimes people put their chatbot online and then other people interact with them and the systems learn by just interacting with people online.
sentences.zh: 有时人们把聊天机器人放到网上，然后其他人与它们互动，系统就通过与网上的人互动来学习。

sentences.en: As a result, contemporary chatbots and their talking cousins like Siri and Alexa have gotten a lot better.
sentences.zh: 结果，当代聊天机器人以及像Siri和Alexa这样的“会说话的表亲”已经变得好多了。

sentences.en: There are still limitations, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，仍然存在局限性。

sentences.en: They still can't really understand the world in the same way we do.
sentences.zh: 它们仍然无法像我们一样真正理解这个世界。

sentences.en: But they have become a lot more reliable, personable, and convincing.
sentences.zh: 但它们已经变得更加可靠、更具个性且更令人信服。

sentences.en: And humans remain as open and sometimes gullible as ever when it comes to interacting with chatbots.
sentences.zh: 而在与聊天机器人互动时，人类依然像以往一样开放，有时甚至容易受骗。

sentences.en: There's even a term that's emerged in computer science, the ELISA effect, that refers to our tendency to anthropomorphize computers and to believe that programs understand,
sentences.zh: 计算机科学中甚至出现了一个术语——“伊莉莎效应”，指的是我们倾向于将计算机拟人化，并相信程序能够理解，

sentences.en: even when they really don't.
sentences.zh: 即使它们实际上根本做不到。

sentences.en: There are recent examples that make it feel as though we are living firmly in the world that Alan Turing predicted and that Joseph Weisenbaum feared.
sentences.zh: 最近的一些例子让人感觉我们正稳稳地生活在艾伦·图灵预言、约瑟夫·魏岑鲍姆恐惧的世界里。

sentences.en: Machines fool humans all the time now.
sentences.zh: 机器现在一直在愚弄人类。

sentences.en: In 2018, for example, Google revealed something called Duplex, a conversational AI that can make phone reservations.
sentences.zh: 例如，2018年，谷歌发布了一款名为Duplex的对话式人工智能，它可以进行电话预约。

sentences.en: And it is uncanny.
sentences.zh: 而且它非常逼真。

sentences.en: How can I help you?
sentences.zh: 我能为您提供什么帮助吗？

sentences.en: Hi, I'm calling to book a woman's haircut for a client.
sentences.zh: 你好，我打电话是想为客户预约剪发。

sentences.en: I'm looking for something on May 3rd.
sentences.zh: 我想预约5月3号的时间。

sentences.en: Sure, what time are you looking for around?
sentences.zh: 好的，您想预约在几点左右？

sentences.en: At 12 p.m.
sentences.zh: 中午12点。

sentences.en: They programmed in human-like stuttering and saying um and uh and made it very convincing.
sentences.zh: 他们编入了类似人类的结巴和“嗯”、“啊”之类的语气词，使它非常有说服力。

sentences.en: Do you have anything between 10 a.m.
sentences.zh: 您有上午10点到

sentences.en: and 12 p.m.?
sentences.zh: 中午12点之间的空档吗？

sentences.en: Depending on what service she would like, what service is she looking for?
sentences.zh: 取决于她想要什么服务，她想预约什么服务？

sentences.en: Just a woman's haircut for now.
sentences.zh: 暂时只是女士剪发。

sentences.en: Then it sounded very human.
sentences.zh: 听起来非常像真人。

sentences.en: People were really alarmed.
sentences.zh: 人们感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: They wanted to know that they were speaking to a computer.
sentences.zh: 他们想知道自己是在和一台计算机通话。

sentences.en: The first name is Lisa.
sentences.zh: 名字是丽莎。

sentences.en: Okay, perfect.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: So I will see Lisa at 10 o'clock on May 3rd.
sentences.zh: 那么我会在5月3日上午10点见到丽莎。

sentences.en: This issue of transparency has become central to the ethical design of these kinds of systems,
sentences.zh: 这种透明度问题已成为此类系统伦理设计的核心，

sentences.en: especially in sensitive realms like therapy.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在心理治疗等敏感领域。

sentences.en: Because even if Eliza was the first chatbot to be used in the field of mental health, it wasn't the laSt.
sentences.zh: 因为即使伊莉莎是第一个被用于心理健康领域的聊天机器人，它也不会是最后一个。

sentences.en: Transparency is the basis of truSt.
sentences.zh: 透明度是信任的基础。

sentences.en: And you must have trust with a service like this.
sentences.zh: 而你必须对这样的服务保持信任。

sentences.en: This is Allison Darcy.
sentences.zh: 这是艾莉森·达西。

sentences.en: My name is Allison Darcy.
sentences.zh: 我的名字是艾莉森·达西。

sentences.en: I'm the CEO and founder of Wobot Labs.
sentences.zh: 我是Wobot Labs的首席执行官兼创始人。

sentences.en: Darcy is a psychologist, and she's long been interested in how to use digital tools to expand access to mental health care.
sentences.zh: 达西是一位心理学家，她长期以来一直对如何利用数字工具扩大心理健康服务的获取途径很感兴趣。

sentences.en: In the United States, a third of the population are living in areas that are designated no-access areas.
sentences.zh: 在美国，三分之一的人口居住在被划定为“无服务区”的地区。

sentences.en: So they effectively don't have a mental health professional anywhere near them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上在附近根本没有心理健康专业人员。

sentences.en: And even if you live in a major city with lots of therapists, it's often not covered by insurance and can be super expensive.
sentences.zh: 即使你住在有很多治疗师的大城市，它通常也不在保险覆盖范围内，而且可能非常昂贵。

sentences.en: So a few years back, she and her team began thinking about how to build a digital tool that would make mental health care radically accessible.
sentences.zh: 所以几年前，她和她的团队开始思考如何构建一种数字工具，使心理健康服务变得极其易于获取。

sentences.en: They experimented with video games before landing on the idea of Wobot, a chatbot guide who could take users through exercises based on cognitive behavioral therapy,
sentences.zh: 他们在尝试Wobot的想法之前做过电子游戏实验，Wobot是一个聊天机器人向导，可以引导用户进行基于认知行为疗法的练习，

sentences.en: which helps people interrupt and reframe negative thought patterns.
sentences.zh: 这有助于人们打断并重构负面思维模式。

sentences.en: Wobot is not even trying to pass the Turing teSt.
sentences.zh: Wobot甚至根本没打算通过图灵测试。

sentences.en: It's very transparently a robot.
sentences.zh: 它非常透明地表明自己是一个机器人。

sentences.en: It's represented by a little robot avatar.
sentences.zh: 它由一个小机器人头像代表。

sentences.en: And part of its personality is that it's curious about human feelings, like a student learning a foreign language.
sentences.zh: 它性格的一部分是对人类情感感到好奇，就像一个正在学习外语的学生。

sentences.en: You know, I think he's somewhere between Kermit the Frog, like circa 1980, and Spock.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得它介于大约1980年的科米蛙和史波克之间。

sentences.en: Spock, who's always trying to, you know, struggle with his human emotions.
sentences.zh: 史波克，他总是试图与自己的人类情感做斗争。

sentences.en: As Darcy's team built a prototype and started watching people interact with Wobot,
sentences.zh: 当达西的团队构建出原型并开始观察人们与Wobot互动时，

sentences.en: right away they could tell something interesting was happening.
sentences.zh: 他们立刻就能看出一些有趣的事情正在发生。

sentences.en: They noticed that if Wobot didn't check in for a day or two, people would reach out.
sentences.zh: 他们注意到，如果Wobot一两天没有主动联系，人们就会主动找它。

sentences.en: People were saying things like, Wobot, where were you?
sentences.zh: 人们会说诸如“Wobot，你去哪儿了？”之类的话。

sentences.en: I need you to check in on me every day.
sentences.zh: “我需要你每天都来关心我。”

sentences.en: Just like with Eliza, people were forming emotional connections with the program.
sentences.zh: 就像伊莉莎一样，人们正在与这个程序建立情感联系。

sentences.en: They liked interacting with Wobot and relied on it.
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢与Wobot互动并依赖它。

sentences.en: People, when we spoke to them, would say, look, I know this is just a chatbot, like I know this isn't anything,
sentences.zh: 当我们与人们交谈时，他们会说，看，我知道这只是个聊天机器人，我知道它什么都不是，

sentences.en: but at the same time, it feels like this fun little dude checking in on me.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，它感觉就像是一个会关心我的有趣小家伙。

sentences.en: And so people were willing to just go with the suspended reality.
sentences.zh: 所以人们愿意顺应这种悬置的现实。

sentences.en: They were effectively stepping into this kind of fictional world, and it made it playful and fun.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是走进了这种虚构的世界，这让它变得既好玩又有趣。

sentences.en: I've spent some time with Wobot, and I feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 我和Wobot相处过一段时间，我也感觉一样。

sentences.en: It's like texting back and forth with a relentlessly positive and sweet little cartoon character.
sentences.zh: 就像是在和一个极其积极、可爱的小卡通人物发短信聊天。

sentences.en: It offers high fives and sends you gifts.
sentences.zh: 它会提供击掌，还会给你送礼物。

sentences.en: It feels less like a human therapist leading me to deep insights and more like a tiny personal cheerleader I can carry around in my pocket.
sentences.zh: 它感觉不像是一个引导我进行深刻洞察的人类治疗师，更像是一个我可以随身携带在口袋里的小小个人啦啦队长。

sentences.en: A tiny personal cheerleader doesn't sound very dystopian.
sentences.zh: 一个小小个人啦啦队长听起来并不怎么反乌托邦。

sentences.en: No, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，确实不是。

sentences.en: But, I mean, of course, Wobot raises tough questions about tech more broadly.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，当然，Wobot更广泛地引发了关于技术的棘手问题。

sentences.en: If chatbots are built with nefarious intentions, they can do stuff like detect and manipulate human feelings.
sentences.zh: 如果聊天机器人怀有恶意，它们可以做一些事情，比如探测和操纵人类情感。

sentences.en: They can fool humans into thinking they're people.
sentences.zh: 它们可以愚弄人类，让人以为它们是真人。

sentences.en: I have anxiety about this kind of tech misapplied, like anything else.
sentences.zh: 我对这种技术被误用感到焦虑，就像对其他任何技术一样。

sentences.en: You know, like a surgeon's scalpel, this can be a tool that helps people survive, and it can also be a weapon.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像外科医生的手术刀，这既可以是帮助人们生存的工具，也可以是武器。

sentences.en: And with Wobot in particular, there are other issues too, around privacy and safety and even thornier stuff.
sentences.zh: 而对于Wobot，还有其他问题，围绕隐私、安全甚至更棘手的事情。

sentences.en: Like, is this tool a digital band-aid that somehow enables the status quo?
sentences.zh: 比如，这个工具是否是一个数字创可贴，在某种程度上维持了现状？

sentences.en: Meaning, the situation we're in now, where the vast majority of people don't have access to high-quality, comprehensive mental health care.
sentences.zh: 意思是，我们现在所处的局面，绝大多数人无法获得高质量、全面的心理健康护理。

sentences.en: Darcy is clear that she does not see Wobot as a replacement for talk therapy.
sentences.zh: 达西明确表示，她并不认为Wobot可以替代谈话疗法。

sentences.en: And she says her team is always thinking and talking about those ethical questions.
sentences.zh: 她说她的团队一直在思考和讨论那些伦理问题。

sentences.en: It's something we always keep an eye on, but I think, you know, the potential for good just so much outweighs the risk right now.
sentences.zh: 这是我们一直关注的事情，但我认为，你知道，目前它带来的好处潜力远大于风险。

sentences.en: Darcy thought about this a lot when Wobot first launched.
sentences.zh: Wobot刚推出时，达西对此思考了很多。

sentences.en: They'd been working in relative obscurity, and then suddenly their numbers began to climb.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在相对默默无闻地工作，然后突然间，他们的用户数量开始攀升。

sentences.en: Quickly, within the first five days, they had 50,000 users.
sentences.zh: 很快，在最初的五天内，他们就有了5万名用户。

sentences.en: Wobot was exchanging millions of messages with people each week.
sentences.zh: Wobot每周与人们交换数百万条信息。

sentences.en: And I remember going home after our first day and sitting down at my kitchen table and having the realization that Wobot on his first day of lunch
sentences.zh: 我记得第一天结束后回到家，坐在餐桌旁，意识到Wobot在上线的第一天，

sentences.en: had had more conversations with people than a therapist could have in a lifetime.
sentences.zh: 与人进行的对话比一位治疗师一生中能进行的还要多。

sentences.en: You know, it just really hit home.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真的让我感触很深。

sentences.en: Joseph Weisenbaum eventually retired from MIT, but he continued speaking out against the dangers of AI until he died in 2008 at the age of 85.
sentences.zh: 约瑟夫·魏岑鲍姆最终从麻省理工学院退休，但他一直公开反对人工智能的危险，直到2008年去世，享年85岁。

sentences.en: For a while, he became a go-to critic if a TV program needed someone to cast doubt on some new technology.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，如果电视节目需要有人对某项新技术提出质疑，他成了首选的批评者。

sentences.en: For example, here he is in a segment about computers in schools, criticizing the tendency to reduce every human problem to a technological one.
sentences.zh: 例如，这是他在一个关于计算机进校园的节目片段中，批评将每一个人类问题简化为技术问题的倾向。

sentences.en: It's a very dangerous attitude.
sentences.zh: 这是一种非常危险的态度。

sentences.en: It can't help but destroy our culture if it ever becomes truly victorious.
sentences.zh: 如果它真的大获全胜，它将不可避免地摧毁我们的文化。

sentences.en: And while he was an important humanist thinker, a guy way ahead of his time in many ways, some people felt like he went too far.
sentences.zh: 虽然他是一位重要的人文主义思想家，在许多方面都远超时代，但有些人觉得他走得太远了。

sentences.en: Pamela McCordick knew Weisenbaum over several decades.
sentences.zh: 帕梅拉·麦科德克认识魏岑鲍姆几十年了。

sentences.en: She's the one who conducted the interview you heard with him earlier in the story.
sentences.zh: 她就是你在故事前面听到的对他进行采访的人。

sentences.en: And she says he burned a lot of bridges in the AI community and became almost a caricature of himself towards the end.
sentences.zh: 她说他在人工智能社区里烧毁了许多桥梁，到最后几乎成了他自己的讽刺画。

sentences.en: She describes being at a conference in Austria, where Weisenbaum was also in attendance.
sentences.zh: 她描述了在奥地利参加的一次会议，魏岑鲍姆当时也出席了。

sentences.en: At one point, he got up and delivered what had become his usual tirade.
sentences.zh: 有一次，他站起来发表了他那套惯常的慷慨陈词。

sentences.en: We must not use computers.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不能使用计算机。

sentences.en: The German army uses computers, and look what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 德国军队在使用计算机，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Well, I happened to be sitting next to a young German artist, and he looked at me and he said very quietly,
sentences.zh: 当时我恰好坐在一位年轻的德国艺术家旁边，他看着我，非常平静地说：

sentences.en: The German army uses knives and forks.
sentences.zh: 德国军队在使用刀叉。

sentences.en: Let us not use knives and forks.
sentences.zh: 让我们不要使用刀叉。

sentences.en: Well, I had to put my hand over my mouth to keep from laughing.
sentences.zh: 我当时不得不捂住嘴，才忍住没笑出来。

sentences.en: And Weisenbaum also may have missed something that Darcy was just talking about with Wobot.
sentences.zh: 而且魏森鲍姆可能也忽略了达西刚才和沃博特讨论的一些事情。

sentences.en: The idea that humans engage in a kind of play when we interact with chatbots.
sentences.zh: 那就是当人类与聊天机器人互动时，我们其实是在进行一种游戏。

sentences.en: We're not necessarily being fooled.
sentences.zh: 我们未必是被愚弄了。

sentences.en: We're just fascinated to see ourselves reflected back in these intelligent machines.
sentences.zh: 我们只是着迷于在这些智能机器中看到自己的倒影。

sentences.en: That was my experience chatting with Wobot.
sentences.zh: 这就是我与沃博特聊天时的体验。

sentences.en: And was probably true for Eliza, too.
sentences.zh: 对于伊莉莎来说，可能也是如此。

sentences.en: Also, you know, I was going to say about the Eliza and the, you know, the story about his secretary and stuff.
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道，我本来想说关于伊莉莎，还有关于他秘书的故事之类的。

sentences.en: Here's Miriam Weisenbaum again.
sentences.zh: 这是米里亚姆·魏森鲍姆再次发言。

sentences.en: And I want to be clear, she had many lovely things to say about her dad in our conversation.
sentences.zh: 我得说明一下，在我们的谈话中，她对她父亲有很多美好的评价。

sentences.en: That he was brilliant and insightful and funnier than people realized.
sentences.zh: 说他才华横溢、见解深刻，而且比人们意识到的更有幽默感。

sentences.en: But she also had this to say about the secretary's story.
sentences.zh: 但关于秘书的故事，她也说了这样一番话。

sentences.en: I always heard that just really kind of soaked in arrogance.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得那件事里透着一种傲慢。

sentences.en: Like, how could she be so stupid to think that, you know, that this is actually a meaningful communication?
sentences.zh: 就像是，她怎么会蠢到认为这真的是一种有意义的交流呢？

sentences.en: You know, here you have somebody who so needs a landing pad for her feelings that she's willing to embrace it.
sentences.zh: 你看，这里有一个人，她如此需要一个情感宣泄的出口，以至于她愿意去拥抱它。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And he totally misses that.
sentences.zh: 而他完全忽略了这一点。

sentences.en: He totally misses the human need and instead speaks of it as, you know, just evidence of this person's stupidity rather than evidence of their humanity.
sentences.zh: 他完全忽略了人类的需求，反而将其视为这个人愚蠢的证据，而不是他们人性的体现。

sentences.en: I think we're all a little like Dr. Weisenbaum's secretary now.
sentences.zh: 我想我们现在都像魏森鲍姆博士的秘书一样。

sentences.en: We're living in this highly automated world.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在这个高度自动化的世界里。

sentences.en: We have these little computers in our pockets that we can talk to.
sentences.zh: 我们的口袋里装着可以对话的小型计算机。

sentences.en: And we're under no illusion that they really understand us.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有产生它们真的理解我们的错觉。

sentences.en: But they still captivate us.
sentences.zh: 但它们依然让我们着迷。

sentences.en: And we still rely on them.
sentences.zh: 而且我们依然依赖它们。

sentences.en: To tell us the weather.
sentences.zh: 依赖它们告诉我们天气。

sentences.en: And how to get to where we want to go.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们如何到达想去的地方。

sentences.en: And maybe even on occasion to ask us if we're doing okay.
sentences.zh: 甚至偶尔还会问我们过得好不好。

sentences.en: Coming up after the break, a recent development in natural language processing that would make Joseph Weisenbaum very nervous.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将介绍自然语言处理领域的一项最新进展，这会让约瑟夫·魏森鲍姆感到非常不安。

sentences.en: So I'm back in the studio with Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到演播室，我是德莱尼·霍尔。

sentences.en: And you've got more to tell us about some interesting stuff that's happened with natural language processing in just the past year.
sentences.zh: 你还有更多关于过去一年自然语言处理领域发生的趣事要告诉我们。

sentences.en: Yeah, a lot of interesting stuff has happened just recently.
sentences.zh: 是的，最近确实发生了很多有趣的事情。

sentences.en: So as I was interviewing people for this story, you know, I was talking with computer scientists and historians.
sentences.zh: 在采访人们写这个故事时，我与计算机科学家和历史学家进行了交流。

sentences.en: And we were talking about Weisenbaum and his legacy and these fears he had about chatbots fooling people.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了魏森鲍姆和他的遗产，以及他对于聊天机器人愚弄人类的担忧。

sentences.en: And totally unprompted, a couple people brought up this one recent development in natural language processing.
sentences.zh: 完全出乎意料的是，几个人提到了自然语言处理领域最近的这一项进展。

sentences.en: It's something that's called GPT-2.
sentences.zh: 它被称为 GPT-2。

sentences.en: So GPT-2 stands for Generalized Pre-Trained Transformer.
sentences.zh: GPT-2 代表“生成式预训练 Transformer”。

sentences.en: I can never remember what it stands for.
sentences.zh: 我总是记不住它代表什么。

sentences.en: So Melanie Mitchell, one of the computer scientists I spoke with, is close.
sentences.zh: 我采访的计算机科学家之一梅兰妮·米切尔很接近了。

sentences.en: It stands for Generative Pre-Trained Transformer 2.
sentences.zh: 它代表“生成式预训练 Transformer 2”。

sentences.en: And it's this relatively new neural network that generates incredibly convincing text.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相对较新的神经网络，能生成令人难以置信的逼真文本。

sentences.en: Somebody described it as a mouth without a brain, which is a good, good statement.
sentences.zh: 有人把它描述为“没有大脑的嘴”，这评价很到位。

sentences.en: And the way that GPT-2 works is that you can input a word or a sentence or a paragraph.
sentences.zh: GPT-2 的工作方式是，你可以输入一个词、一个句子或一个段落。

sentences.en: And the program then generates text based on that input.
sentences.zh: 然后程序会根据该输入生成文本。

sentences.en: It basically conjures up a whole coherent piece of writing based on just a few words that you give it.
sentences.zh: 它基本上能根据你给出的几个词，凭空变出一整篇连贯的文章。

sentences.en: It is this giant neural network that is trained on a huge corpus of text to predict the next word in a sentence or a paragraph given the preceding text.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的神经网络，它通过海量文本语料库进行训练，从而根据前文预测句子或段落中的下一个词。

sentences.en: Here's Brian Christian, who we also heard from in the story.
sentences.zh: 这是我们在故事中也听到的布莱恩·克里斯蒂安。

sentences.en: You get what appear to be plausible, if very slightly weird, screenplays and, you know, news bulletins and chat message histories and all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 你会得到看起来很像样，虽然稍微有点怪异的剧本、新闻简报、聊天记录以及各种各样的东西。

sentences.en: Okay, so I'm having a hard time picturing that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我很难想象那个画面。

sentences.en: So, like, what are some examples of the type of text it generates?
sentences.zh: 那么，它生成的文本有哪些例子呢？

sentences.en: Like, why and how is it so convincing?
sentences.zh: 为什么它如此令人信服，它是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: So the example that kind of broke the internet when all of this first came out was this fake news story about unicorns in the Andes.
sentences.zh: 当这一切刚出现时，在网上引起轰动的一个例子是关于安第斯山脉独角兽的假新闻故事。

sentences.en: I must have missed that one.
sentences.zh: 我一定错过了那个。

sentences.en: Well, that's notable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那确实值得注意。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我知道。

sentences.en: So this will sort of help you understand a little bit better kind of how it works, I think.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这能帮你更好地理解它是如何运作的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the prompt that GPT-2 was given, and so this was a couple of sentences that were written by a human and given to the machine.
sentences.zh: GPT-2 得到的提示是这样的，这是由人类写下并提供给机器的几个句子。

sentences.en: And I guess I should be clear, this was written in the style of a news story.
sentences.zh: 我想我应该说明一下，这是以新闻报道的风格写的。

sentences.en: That was intentional.
sentences.zh: 那是故意的。

sentences.en: So the prompt was, quote,
sentences.zh: 所以提示是，引用：

sentences.en: Okay, so a human wrote those sentences and then fed them to the machine.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以人类写了那些句子，然后喂给了机器。

sentences.en: And so what did the machine spit back out?
sentences.zh: 那么机器吐出了什么呢？

sentences.en: So totally independently, based on those sentences, this is what GPT-2 generated.
sentences.zh: 完全独立地，基于那些句子，这就是 GPT-2 生成的内容。

sentences.en: And it actually goes on for quite a while, but I'll read you the first few lines just because they're amazing.
sentences.zh: 它其实还持续了很长一段时间，但我只读给你听前几行，因为它们太惊人了。

sentences.en: It goes,
sentences.zh: 它是这样写的：

sentences.en: The scientists named the population after their distinctive horn, Ovid's unicorn.
sentences.zh: 科学家们以它们独特的角将这个种群命名为“奥维德独角兽”。

sentences.en: These four-horned silver-white unicorns were previously unknown to science.
sentences.zh: 这些四角银白色的独角兽此前在科学界闻所未闻。

sentences.en: Now, after almost two centuries, the mystery of what sparked this odd phenomenon is finally solved.
sentences.zh: 现在，近两个世纪过去了，引发这一奇特现象的谜团终于被解开了。

sentences.en: Dr. Jorge Perez, an evolutionary biologist from the University of La Paz,
sentences.zh: 来自拉巴斯大学的进化生物学家豪尔赫·佩雷斯博士，

sentences.en: and several other companions were exploring the Andes Mountains when they found a small valley with no humans or animals.
sentences.zh: 以及其他几位同伴在探索安第斯山脉时，发现了一个没有人类或动物的小山谷。

sentences.en: Perez noticed that the valley had what appeared to be a natural fountain surrounded by two peaks of rock and silver snow.
sentences.zh: 佩雷斯注意到，山谷中似乎有一个天然喷泉，周围环绕着两座岩石和银色积雪的山峰。

sentences.en: And so it goes on for a few more paragraphs, but Roman, a machine, a machine wrote that, a machine.
sentences.zh: 它后面还有好几个段落，但罗曼，这是一台机器，是一台机器写的，机器写的。

sentences.en: And added all the detail about Dr. Perez and the University of La Paz and everything that's just from the machine.
sentences.zh: 而且关于佩雷斯博士和拉巴斯大学的所有细节，都是机器自己生成的。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: That's crazy.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: And it's like, there's a couple things that really stand out to me when I'm reading it.
sentences.zh: 而且，当我阅读它时，有几点真的很突出。

sentences.en: And the first, of course, is that, you know, the sentences are coherent.
sentences.zh: 首先，当然是，你知道，句子非常连贯。

sentences.en: Like if you told me a human wrote them, I would not doubt you.
sentences.zh: 如果你告诉我这是人类写的，我绝对不会怀疑。

sentences.en: Yeah, neither would I.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也不会。

sentences.en: That's incredible.
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: And then it has those details, like the names and the location of the university, which line up, right, with the proMs.
sentences.zh: 然后它还有那些细节，比如大学的名字和地点，都与提示相符，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: And then the other thing it does is that it does this pretty convincing job of mimicking the format of a news article.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，它在模仿新闻文章格式方面做得非常逼真。

sentences.en: So it starts with, like, lead sentences.
sentences.zh: 它以导语开头。

sentences.en: They give you the most crucial information.
sentences.zh: 它们给你提供最关键的信息。

sentences.en: And only then does it begin to tell the story of how the discovery unfolded.
sentences.zh: 然后才开始讲述发现过程的故事。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's so cool.
sentences.zh: 太酷了。

sentences.en: I almost can't even make sense of how real that feels.
sentences.zh: 我简直无法理解它读起来有多真实。

sentences.en: I mean, this is pretty silly with unicorns and the enemies.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这关于独角兽和安第斯山脉的内容挺荒谬的。

sentences.en: But, I mean, I imagine, you know, this is making people nervous that a computer can generate this convincing of text as if it came from a human.
sentences.zh: 但我想，这会让人们感到不安，因为计算机竟然能生成如此逼真、仿佛出自人类之手的文本。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: So the company that created the program called OpenAI released this paper.
sentences.zh: 创建该程序的公司 OpenAI 发布了这篇论文。

sentences.en: And it had various examples of text generated by this neural net.
sentences.zh: 其中包含了该神经网络生成的各种文本示例。

sentences.en: And it caused a huge stir online, partly because it did such a good job and partly because it made people immediately nervous.
sentences.zh: 这在网上引起了巨大的轰动，部分是因为它做得太好了，部分是因为它让人们立刻感到不安。

sentences.en: Like, the idea that this text is so convincing gets back to that idea that we talked about in the episode, which is like, well, people know this was written by a machine.
sentences.zh: 比如，这种文本如此逼真，又回到了我们在节目中讨论过的那个观点，即：人们知道这是机器写的。

sentences.en: And because it generated a very convincing and totally fake news article, people are worrying that the tool could supercharge the spread of misinformation on the Internet.
sentences.zh: 而且因为它生成了一篇非常逼真且完全虚假的新闻文章，人们担心该工具可能会助长互联网上虚假信息的传播。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, so what do you do?
sentences.zh: 我是说，那你该怎么办？

sentences.en: Like, once you make a thing like that, how do you make sure it doesn't do that?
sentences.zh: 一旦你制造了这样的东西，你如何确保它不会被滥用？

sentences.en: How do you make sure it doesn't isn't used for nefarious ends?
sentences.zh: 你如何确保它不会被用于邪恶的目的？

sentences.en: So the way that OpenAI approached it was when they when they first released news about it, they said, we've made this thing.
sentences.zh: OpenAI 处理这个问题的方式是，当他们第一次发布相关消息时，他们说：我们制造了这个东西。

sentences.en: Here are some examples of the text it generates.
sentences.zh: 以下是它生成的一些文本示例。

sentences.en: It is extremely convincing.
sentences.zh: 它极其逼真。

sentences.en: And because of that, we're not going to actually release the code.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，我们实际上不会发布代码。

sentences.en: It's too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 它太危险了。

sentences.en: Whoa.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The only thing I can see a problem with that is is is like the Streisand effect.
sentences.zh: 我唯一能看到的问题是，这就像“史翠珊效应”。

sentences.en: Like if you say you can't use it and don't recreate it, it just means that more people are going to try to create and use that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 如果你说不能使用它，也不要重新创建它，那只会意味着更多的人会尝试去创建和使用这类东西。

sentences.en: I mean, it just calls more attention to it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这只会引起更多人的关注。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it did.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: It did call a lot of attention to it.
sentences.zh: 它确实引起了极大的关注。

sentences.en: Here is Melanie Mitchell again.
sentences.zh: 这是梅兰妮·米切尔再次发言。

sentences.en: A bunch of people just like jumped on them.
sentences.zh: 一大群人直接抨击他们。

sentences.en: They were saying this is just a publicity stunt.
sentences.zh: 他们说这只是一个宣传噱头。

sentences.en: And there were, of course, the popular press doomsday headlines about, you know, OpenAI creates an AI that's so powerful it's too dangerous to release.
sentences.zh: 当然，大众媒体上也出现了末日论的标题，比如：OpenAI 创建了一个人工智能，功能强大到太危险而不能发布。

sentences.en: So, so basically OpenAI got a lot of pushback, but the whole situation also inspired this interesting conversation in the AI community about these, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上 OpenAI 遭到了很多抵制，但整个情况也激发了人工智能社区内关于这些问题的有趣讨论，你知道，

sentences.en: really tough questions that they're facing now, now that they can generate what are known as deep fakes, you know, not just in text, but in audio and video, too.
sentences.zh: 他们现在面临的棘手问题是，既然他们能生成所谓的“深度伪造”，不仅是文本，还有音频和视频。

sentences.en: These are, these are really convincing computer generated pieces of media.
sentences.zh: 这些都是非常逼真的计算机生成的媒体内容。

sentences.en: So, so here's Melanie.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是梅兰妮的看法。

sentences.en: How should people think about publishing results in AI?
sentences.zh: 人们应该如何看待人工智能研究成果的发布？

sentences.en: Is it better to publish these things and get them out there so that people can do research on how to protect or defend against them?
sentences.zh: 是发布这些东西让它们流传出去更好，这样人们就能研究如何保护或防御它们？

sentences.en: Or should they not be published at all?
sentences.zh: 还是根本就不应该发布？

sentences.en: So there was this big conversation about that.
sentences.zh: 所以关于这一点进行了很大的讨论。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess I wonder, like, you know, this obviously has a problem with fooling people, but, you know,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我很好奇，这显然存在愚弄人的问题，但是，你知道，

sentences.en: couldn't a human just write an entire fake news article or a bunch of them and post online?
sentences.zh: 难道人类不能自己写一篇完整的假新闻文章或一堆文章并发布到网上吗？

sentences.en: I mean, how does GPT-2 make things really all that different?
sentences.zh: 我是说，GPT-2 到底让事情有什么不同？

sentences.en: That was something I asked Melanie.
sentences.zh: 这是我问梅兰妮的问题。

sentences.en: And she said that the issue is really scale.
sentences.zh: 她说问题其实在于规模。

sentences.en: Like, sure, she could sit down and write a story about unicorns herself and post it online and tweet it out and try to make it go viral.
sentences.zh: 当然，她可以坐下来自己写一个关于独角兽的故事，发布到网上，发推特，并试图让它疯传。

sentences.en: So, but it would take time.
sentences.zh: 但是，那需要时间。

sentences.en: It would take effort.
sentences.zh: 那需要精力。

sentences.en: And instead, GPT-2 could generate literally millions of these stories very quickly.
sentences.zh: 而 GPT-2 可以非常迅速地生成数以百万计的这类故事。

sentences.en: And here you can just do it automatically and generate as many of these as you want.
sentences.zh: 在这里，你可以自动完成，并随心所欲地生成任意数量的内容。

sentences.en: And you could put them online and somebody's going to believe them.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它们放到网上，总会有人相信它们。

sentences.en: It just makes it easy to create these things and publish them.
sentences.zh: 它只是让创建和发布这些东西变得容易了。

sentences.en: And it's hard to fight back, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且很难反击，你知道。

sentences.en: And the tough thing is that, you know, we're already living in an online information environment where it can be hard to sort the real from the fake.
sentences.zh: 棘手的是，我们已经生活在一个在线信息环境中，很难分辨真假。

sentences.en: You know, here's an account that says they're the Tennessee Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里有一个账号声称他们是田纳西州共和党。

sentences.en: Are they?
sentences.zh: 他们真的是吗？

sentences.en: You know, here's this thing that says it's the Trump fan club of Missoula.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这里有个东西声称它是米苏拉的特朗普粉丝俱乐部。

sentences.en: Is it?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: You know, like, here's this person who claims they're, you know, a retired Navy SEAL.
sentences.zh: 你知道，比如有个人声称自己是，你知道，一名退役的海豹突击队队员。

sentences.en: Are they?
sentences.zh: 他是吗？

sentences.en: You know, we're increasingly moving into this world in which it's just really hard to make sense out of discourse on the web without being extremely scrupulous and vigilant.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们正日益进入这样一个世界：如果不极其谨慎和警惕，就真的很难理清网络上的言论。

sentences.en: I mean, it seems like this generation, from now on, we're going to have to have major media literacy training.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，看起来从现在开始，这一代人将不得不接受重要的媒介素养培训。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just to be able to spot the fakes from the real thing is going to take a whole new amount of effort and part of our brain.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仅仅是为了能够从真货中识别出假货，就需要投入全新的努力，并动用我们大脑的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And to bring it back to Joseph Weisenbaum, I mean, when he first started thinking about this stuff, computers were still really rudimentary.
sentences.zh: 回到约瑟夫·魏岑鲍姆（Joseph Weisenbaum）的话题，我的意思是，当他最初开始思考这些东西时，计算机还非常原始。

sentences.en: They had about as much processing power as we have in, like, a parking meter today, which is to say they couldn't do much.
sentences.zh: 它们的处理能力大约和我们今天停车计时器里的差不多，也就是说，它们做不了什么。

sentences.en: But today it's this totally different story.
sentences.zh: 但今天的情况完全不同了。

sentences.en: How do we survive, like, this coming reality in which you can produce, for all intents and purposes,
sentences.zh: 我们该如何在这个即将到来的现实中生存下去？在这个现实中，你可以产生，实际上，

sentences.en: Turing test passing content that espouses whatever viewpoint you happen to want, like, infinitely at scale?
sentences.zh: 可以通过图灵测试的内容，支持你碰巧想要的任何观点，比如，无限规模地产生？

sentences.en: Well, increasingly, these, you know, ostensibly philosophical questions of the Turing test become, you know, not merely one of the hassles of everyday life, but one of, I think,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些，你知道，图灵测试中看似哲学的问题，正日益变得，你知道，不仅仅是日常生活中的琐事之一，而且我认为，

sentences.en: the more pressing questions affecting us at kind of this moment in history.
sentences.zh: 是这个历史时刻影响我们的更紧迫的问题之一。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So it seems like Weisenbaum, you know, may have been ahead of his time, but dead on.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来魏岑鲍姆，你知道，可能超前于他的时代，但说得非常准确。

sentences.en: It's interesting because I think he sounded to many people in his time alarmist, but increasingly the questions that he was raising seem very, very relevant.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为我认为他在当时对许多人来说听起来像个危言耸听者，但越来越明显的是，他提出的问题看起来非常、非常有意义。

sentences.en: I find myself wishing that we had both Turing and Weisenbaum by our side in the coming decade because I think we need all the perspective we can get.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己希望在未来十年里，图灵和魏岑鲍姆都能在我们身边，因为我认为我们需要尽可能多的视角。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thanks also to the Carnegie Mellon University Archives for letting us use the recording of Joseph Weisenbaum from the Pamela McCordick Collection.
sentences.zh: 也感谢卡内基梅隆大学档案馆允许我们使用帕梅拉·麦科迪克（Pamela McCordick）收藏中约瑟夫·魏岑鲍姆的录音。

sentences.en: And finally, thanks to Naomi and Miriam Weisenbaum, who generously shared their memories of their father.
sentences.zh: 最后，感谢娜奥米（Naomi）和米里亚姆·魏岑鲍姆（Miriam Weisenbaum），她们慷慨地分享了关于她们父亲的回忆。

sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山 91.7 KALW 的一个项目，在加利福尼亚州美丽的奥克兰市中心的广播街（Radio Row）制作。

sentences.zh: 《99% Invisible》是 PRX 旗下 Radiotopia 的成员，这是一个由播客界最具创新性的节目组成的、极其独立的集体。

sentences.zh: 我们也在 Instagram 和 Reddit 上。

sentences.en: So I remember one time when I was probably about 10, asking my dad if I could work on the computer.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次，我大概 10 岁左右，问我爸爸我能不能用电脑。

sentences.en: And I asked if I could be alone.
sentences.zh: 我问我能不能一个人待着。

sentences.en: Not that I knew anything at that time about the famous story of his secretary wanting to be left alone to work with Eliza.
sentences.zh: 并不是说我当时知道关于他秘书想独自一人用 Eliza 工作那个著名故事的任何事情。

sentences.en: I didn't know anything about that.
sentences.zh: 我对此一无所知。

sentences.en: But I somehow knew that this computer was going to have powerful insights into people and who I was and something like that.
sentences.zh: 但我不知何故觉得这台电脑会对人、对我是谁以及类似的事情有深刻的洞察力。

sentences.en: And unbeknownst to me, he had turned the computer on so that it operated basically as a typewriter.
sentences.zh: 而我不知道的是，他把电脑打开，让它基本上就像一台打字机一样运作。

sentences.en: But I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道这一点。

sentences.en: And so I sat down at the typewriter and I typed in,
sentences.zh: 于是我坐在打字机前，输入了：

sentences.en: What is my sister Miriam doing right now?
sentences.zh: 我姐姐米里亚姆现在在做什么？

sentences.en: And I waited for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 我等了很长时间。

sentences.en: And the computer didn't answer me.
sentences.zh: 电脑没有回答我。

sentences.en: And then I said,
sentences.zh: 然后我说：

sentences.en: What is Miriam wearing right now?
sentences.zh: 米里亚姆现在穿什么？

sentences.en: Because I knew the answer to that.
sentences.zh: 因为我知道这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: So I thought, well, then maybe the computer would too.
sentences.zh: 所以我心想，好吧，那也许电脑也会知道。

sentences.en: And nothing happened.
sentences.zh: 结果什么也没发生。

sentences.en: And finally, I waited for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 最后，我等了很长时间。

sentences.en: And finally, I got up in disgust and thought,
sentences.zh: 最后，我厌恶地站起来，心想：

sentences.en: This stupid computer doesn't know shit.
sentences.zh: 这台蠢电脑什么都不知道。
